chapter: Meeting Jay McShann and Martin's on the Plaza
title: McShann played down on the Charlie Parker package tour
summary: McShann was hurt when a tour presented a Parker authority as the star; Dance says George Wein's package flopped in Berlin.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I'll tell you what happened and he told me -- he thinks it's the jokers in his life. I won't call it a name, but he had a tour with somebody, and I think they went behind the Iron Curtain.

And he told me, he said, these guys, you probably know who I'm talking about, played him down so low, he says it just was getting to him, nightly, you know. This guy was getting up, he was the authority on Byrd, and he was the authority on how the Byrd learned to play. And like McShann was just another man in the band.
He said it really tore him up. I don't know whether George Wein booked them over there or not.
Well, I'm just trying to think, Gene. He went in that stupid package.

That Charlie Parker package. Now, he went in there and, you know, that was another ridiculous thing, because George Wein took Billy Eckstein, who comes on singing ballads, I think it was in Berlin they booed Billy Eckstein off.
